name: Benin court brass casting: royal commemorative head
description: Specialist artists in the Benin kingdom produced cast-brass royal representations under court patronage.

impact.note: Court-bound casting for one kingdom's palace, refining an existing regional lost-wax craft; later Benin court casting continued from it.

date.label: early fifteenth to mid-sixteenth century, approximately
date.basis: The current catalogue dates the exact object to early fifteenth–mid-sixteenth century; 1400–1550 is an approximate indexing envelope, not a measured chronology. The older educators catalogue gives circa 1550.

events.statement: A cast-brass royal commemorative head is attributed to Benin brass-casting guild artists and dated by the current Met catalogue to the early fifteenth–mid-sixteenth century.
events.scope: A dated object witness, not the origin of the guild or lost-wax casting. The current catalogue has a broader interval than the earlier educators publication.

evidence.supports: The museum describes a mid-sixteenth-century royal head and guilds working under royal patronage.

evidence.locator: Object 1979.206.86, Artwork Details and curatorial description
evidence.supports: Identifies the object, artist guild, broader date interval and royal ancestral use.
